Maria: quick sync — replay harness for the customer workload is showing ~18% worse p95 latency than our synthetic runs with the same qps/profile. anyone else seeing this discrepancy?
Vikram: can you paste the run commands + model/kernel flags? might be a kernel selection or batching mismatch.
Maria: here are the two commands i ran — synth vs replay: 
```
# synthetic
./bench --profile=webchat_short --qps=120 --warmup=60 --kernel-autoselect
# replay
./replay_harness --trace=trace_2026-03-10.pb --speed=1.0 --warmup=0 --kernel-autoselect
```
Maria: note: replay run had warmup=0 (intentional to test cold-start behavior). but that may be the culprit — kv-cache hit rate was low.
Sanjay: low kv-cache hits will blow up TTFT and p95. do you have kv cache hit logs?
Maria: yep — snippet from runtime profile (replay run): 
```
KV_CACHE_LOOKUP: 42% time, hit_rate=0.12
SELECT_KERNEL: 18% time
APPLY_BATCHING: 14% time
TOKEN_GEN: 26% time
```
Vikram: interesting — SELECT_KERNEL at 18% suggests kernel decision code is running often (maybe because model variant selection changed after cold prefixes). in synth runs our kernel decision is amortized (warm cache).
Kate: to be explicit on metrics so we're apples-to-apples: 
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) = time from request arrival to first token emitted by model
- TPOT (time-per-output-token) = avg time to produce each subsequent token after first
- p95/p99 refer to the distribution of TTFT unless we specify otherwise
- goodput = tokens successfully generated per second that meet latency SLO; QPS is request frequency.
Vikram: +1 on Kate. also make sure when we compare p95 we use the same aggregation window and exclude warmup.
Eli: my hypothesis: replay trace includes a lot of short-turn chats which prevent KV cache from warming (different prefixes) — synthetic profile used a small set of reusey prefixes. so batching heuristics also see different seq-len distributions.
Maria: we profiled batch composition: replay produced many 1-2 token reply requests, which made batching less efficient and increased per-request overhead.
Sanjay: actionable checklist: 
1) re-run replay with warmup=60 to let KV cache and kernels stabilize
2) pin kernel selection to the same kernel used in synthetic to measure kernel-only delta: `--kernel=triton_fast_fp16`
3) capture TTFT and TPOT histograms separately, and log kv-cache hit rates and batch sizes per-second
bench-bot: scheduled job #r-2301: replay_warmup60 pinned-kernel, 50k reqs, outputs -> /runs/r-2301
Vikram: also add a small change to the harness: force batching window to 4ms to mimic synth's batching aggressiveness (synthetic harness had a 4ms max-latency window).
Kate: reminder on analysis: when we report p95 we should state whether it's TTFT-p95 or token-p95. also include goodput delta and raw QPS. customers care about p95 TTFT and goodput.
Maria: i'll kick off the three runs (cold replay, warm replay, warm pinned) and post results in this thread. expected run time ~30m.
Eli: if we see kernel-selection dominating once warm, then we should consider caching kernel choice per-model+seqlen bucket. reduces SELECT_KERNEL overhead.
Sanjay: and if kv-cache warming is the main factor, we should add a standard 'trace prewarm' step to the replay harness docs. that will help apples-to-apples comparisons across teams.
Maria: thanks — will update the benchmark SOP with a prewarm step and explicit metric definitions (TTFT, TPOT, goodput vs QPS). will @everyone when results are in. :thumbsup:
